reason: The flat 1.2% stop was 0.92x to 0.98x the dislocation being faded, so noise in the gap itself took the position out before the thesis could resolve. There was also no stand down after a stop, so the engine re-entered the same symbol on the next tick.
note: Structural fix, made after two losing trades exposed it. Position size derives from the stop, so a wider stop means a smaller clip and unchanged risk per trade. Disclosed here rather than quietly applied; split the log at this timestamp when judging the strategy.

change: opening halted, strategy retired on evidence
reason: The live log falsified the thesis. Basis converged in 8 of 10 closed trades and all 10 still lost money. A single leg perpetual position is exposed to price, not to the spread the thesis is about, so convergence delivered nothing: it happened via the index moving toward the mark rather than the mark moving toward the index. Two trades exited on TAKE_PROFIT, meaning basis reached target, and still lost.

attribution.note: Fees are 6% of the loss. This was not a cost problem. It was directional exposure on instruments where the strategy had no directional edge.

alternativesConsidered.cashAndCarry: Short perp plus long spot is delta neutral and would fix the exposure mismatch. Only 30 perps have a spot leg above $10M volume, funding on those is about 1 bps per 8h (~11%/yr), so roughly 3 bps a day against a round trip cost near 24 bps. It does not clear costs before the deadline. The extreme funding names are negative funding, which needs long perp plus short spot, and spot borrow is not available.
alternativesConsidered.rebuildDirectional: Rejected. Choosing a new strategy after observing losses, with no validated edge and a sample of ten, is curve fitting.

effect: The engine keeps ticking, marking open positions to market and exiting them under the existing rules. It opens nothing new. Opening is a gate check named opening-enabled, so refusals appear in decisions.jsonl like any other.

change: strategy v1 retired, v2 delta neutral basis arbitrage live
reason: v1 held one leg of a two leg idea. Basis converged in 8 of 10 trades and all 10 lost, $7,444 of the $7,724 from directional price movement against $432 of fees. Two exits hit their basis target and still lost. Root cause confirmed from the log: convergence came from the index moving toward the mark, so a perpetual-only position earned none of it. Compounding it, a 25bps trigger selected instruments whose mark and index diverge structurally rather than from mispricing; six of the nine traded have no spot listing at all and several are tokenised equity perpetuals whose index goes stale when the underlying market closes.
fix: v2 requires a tradeable spot leg, trades only the direction hedgeable without borrow (perp rich to spot), and holds both legs so the position earns convergence rather than direction. Exits are convergence, divergence stop and max hold. There is no directional stop because there is no directional exposure.

measuredConsequence.note: The fix is correct and it reveals the market is efficient net of taker costs. Three avenues were tested against live books.
measuredConsequence.gapArbitrage: 0 of 343 pairs clear cost at any volume floor from $10M down to zero. Wider gaps carry proportionally wider spreads, so cost scales with the dislocation.
measuredConsequence.fundingCarry: 0 of 76 liquid positive funding pairs are profitable over the 5 days remaining. Funding is 5 to 11 percent annualised, earning 7 to 15 bps against 24 to 45 bps of round trip cost.
measuredConsequence.hedgeableDirection: Large dislocations are almost always perp cheap, which would need spot borrow. The hedgeable direction rarely carries a large gap.

effect: The gate stays live and will fire automatically if a dislocation or funding spike clears cost during the remaining window. On ticks where it opens nothing it now records the edge distribution across the scanned universe, so the refusal is quantified rather than merely counted.
equityContinuity: The equity curve is not reset. v1's losses stay in the record and trades carry their strategy tag, so the two regimes can be evaluated separately from one continuous log.

reason: The local session and the GitHub Actions runner both ticked during the v1 to v2 transition, and each independently closed VTHOUSDT. Naively merging would have double counted that close.
method: State was rebuilt from the union of trades.jsonl rather than from either side's state.json, keeping the earliest close per position id because the first close is the one that actually happened. Equity and decision logs were unioned by timestamp and deduped. Realised PnL was then recomputed from the reconciled closed trades.
note: Disclosed rather than silently resolved. The arithmetic is reproducible from trades.jsonl.
